items.title: Now the voting cards are coming - digitally
items.summary: For the first time this year, Swedish voters will be able to make their choices with digital voting cards that will be sent to the digital mailboxes starting today, Saturday. The news affects around 6.5 million people, according to the Norwegian Electoral Authority. But neither digital nor physical voting cards are needed anymore.
items.summary_original: För första gången ska svenska väljare i år kunna göra sina val med digitala röstkort som skickas till de digitala brevlådorna med start i dag, lördag. Nyheten berör omkring 6,5 miljoner personer, enligt Valmyndigheten. Men varken digitala eller fysiska röstkort behövs längre.

items.title: The US tests the loyalty of NATO countries with questionnaires - interpreted as blackmail
items.summary: Has the country supported the Iran war? Will it do business with American defense companies? The US has sent a questionnaire to its NATO allies to test loyalty. Something that the recipient countries consider blackmail.
items.title_original: USA testar Natoländernas lojalitet med frågeformulär – tolkas som utpressning
items.summary_original: Har landet stöttat Irankriget? Kommer man att handla med amerikanska försvarsföretag? USA har skickat ett frågeformulär till sina Natoallierade för att testa lojaliteten. Något som mottagarländerna anser vara utpressning.

items.title: Astronomer found dead - accused of extensive cheating
items.summary: Last week, Jason Arday left his professorship at Cambridge University in England. The origin was that the young star researcher was singled out for extensive plagiarism and cheating. "Incessant accusations, speculation and public comments have taken a toll on both me and those I love," Arday said in a statement in connection with the dismissal, The Guardian reports. On Friday, Arday was found dead in his home. According to British media, he was unconscious when he was found by paramedics, and he was later pronounced dead at the scene. 30 marathons in 35 days In 2023, the then 37-year-old Jason Arday became the youngest black professor at Cambridge ever. The whole thing was seen as somewhat spectacular when Arday himself stated that due to his autism he could neither read nor write until he was 18 years old. Arday has also claimed to have run 30 marathons in 35 days and to have run nearly 1,000 kilometers in six days. However, his feats have been questioned many times in the past and Arday himself has changed his stories on several occasions. At the end of July, Arday found himself in the spotlight again when Nathan Cofnas, a former professor at Cambridge, pointed out extensive plagiarism in Arday's doctoral thesis. Accusations against Arday were also made by David Harris, professor emeritus at Cambridge. According to The Telegraph, over 100 suspected plagiarisms have been found in the text. But the criticism and accusations against Arday remained and a few weeks later, Cambridge announced that they had opened an investigation into Arday's qualifications as "new evidence emerged". items.title_original: Stjärnforskaren hittad död – anklagades för omfattande fusk
items.summary_original: I förra veckan lämnade Jason Arday sin professorstjänst på Cambridgeuniversitetet i England. Upprinnelsen var att den unge stjärnforskaren pekats ut för omfattande plagiering och fusk. ”Oupphörliga anklagelser, spekulationer och offentliga kommentarer har tagit hårt på både mig och dem jag älskar”, sa Arday i ett uttalande i samband med uppsägningen, rapporterar The Guardian. På fredagen hittades Arday död i sitt hem. Enlig brittiska medier var han medvetslös när han hittades av ambulanspersonal, och han förklarades senare död på platsen. 30 maraton på 35 dagar 2023 blev den då 37-årige Jason Arday den yngste svarta professorn på Cambridge någonsin. Det hela sågs smått spektakulärt då Arday själv uppget att han på grund av sin autism varken kunde läsa eller skriva förrän han var 18 år. Arday har även påstått att han sprungit 30 maraton på 35 dagar och att han sprungit nästan 1 000 kilometer på sex dagar. Hans bragder har dock ifrågasatts många gånger tidigare och Arday har själv ändrat sina historier vid flera tillfällen. I slutet av juli hamnade Arday i rampljuset på nytt när Nathan Cofnas, tidigare professor vid Cambridge, pekade ut omfattande plagiering i Ardays doktorsavhandling. Anklagelser mot Arday riktades även från David Harris, professor emeritus vid Cambridge. Enligt The Telegraph ska över 100 misstänkta plagiat ha hittats i texten. Inledde egen utredning Både Cofnas och Harris anses kontroversiella och Cambridge tog därför först Arday i försvar och kallade uttalandena för ”en vidrig smutskastningskampanj för att undergräva hans trovärdighet”, rapporterar The Guardian.  Men kritiken och anklagelserna mot Arday fanns kvar och någon vecka senare meddelade Cambridge att de inlett en utredning av Ardays kvalifikationer då ”nya bevis framkommit”. Samma kväll som uttalandet från universitet släpptes meddelade Arday att han lämnar sin tjänst. ”Det enda sättet att avsluta det här kapitlet är att kliva åt sidan”, sa Arday i ett utlåtande. Familjen: ”Lång kampanj av trakasserier” Drygt en vecka efter att ha lämnat sin tjänst hittades Arday död. Polisen utreder dödsfallet, men misstänker i nuläget inget brott, rapporterar BBC. Familjen skriver i ett uttalande att Arday utsatts för en lång kampanj av trakasserier från personer som ”inte skyr några medel i sina försök att undergräva honom” ända sedan han började sin tjänst vid Cambridge. ”Vi är chockerade över att ha förlorat denne fantastiske far, partner, bror, farbror och son”, skriver familjen.

items.title: Sweden provides SEK 5 million in humanitarian assistance to Colombia following earthquake
items.summary: Sweden has announced SEK 5 million in humanitarian support to Colombia through the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) following the earthquake that recently hit the country. This will help address urgent humanitarian needs, strengthen support for people who have been forced to leave their homes and provide assistance to the most vulnerable groups in affected areas. Through the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), Sweden has long been a key donor of humanitarian assistance to Colombia.

items.title: Maria Malmer Stenergard visits Latin America
items.summary: In turbulent times, Sweden’s ties with the countries of Latin America become all the more important. Sweden has extensive interests in the region and is engaged in several forms of close cooperation that the Government intends to further solidify, not least with Brazil and Colombia. The visit also gave Minister of Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard the opportunity to emphasise the importance of continued support to Ukraine during talks with her Latin American counterparts.

items.title: Sweden deepens cooperation with Brazil
items.summary: On Wednesday, in connection with Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard’s visit to Brazil, the two countries signed a bilateral action plan for expanded cooperation. This signing took place against the backdrop of Sweden and Brazil celebrating 200 years of diplomatic relations this year.

items.title: Sweden opens Consulate-General in Munich
items.summary: The Government has decided to open a consulate-general in southern Germany’s largest city, Munich. The aim is to help create higher growth in Sweden, strengthen Swedish competitiveness and increase interest in Sweden as an investment destination. Germany is Sweden’s most important trading partner and the world’s third-largest economy. Southern Germany is the country’s economic and political centre after the capital Berlin.

items.title: Minister for Foreign Affairs to visit Latin America
items.summary: On 5–7 August, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard is visiting Brazil and Colombia. During the visit, Ms Malmer Stenergard is meeting with government representatives in the region and attending the presidential inauguration in Colombia.

items.title: Sweden strengthens Ukraine’s health and medical care through partnership and Swedish expertise
items.summary: Russia’s full-scale invasion has put Ukraine’s health and medical system under severe pressure at the same time as care needs have increased sharply. The Government is therefore allocating SEK 6.9 million to the Swecare Foundation for 2026 to strengthen Ukraine’s health care. This is being done through training initiatives, knowledge exchange and partnerships between Swedish and Ukrainian actors, including in the business sector.
